Krippendorff's \(\alpha\) Inter-Rater Agreement

Source: R/krippendorff_alpha.R
krippendorff_alpha.Rd

Computes Krippendorff's (1980, 2004, 2011) \(\alpha\), a chance-corrected inter-rater agreement coefficient. Unlike cohen_kappa (two raters; nominal categories, or ordinal ones through weights) or fleiss_kappa (multiple raters, nominal categories, no missing ratings), Krippendorff's \(\alpha\) supports any number of raters, missing values, and any of four levels of measurement (nominal, ordinal, interval, ratio) via a user-specified distance metric.

Usage

krippendorff_alpha(
  ratings,
  level = c("nominal", "ordinal", "interval", "ratio"),
  conf_level = 0.95,
  boot = FALSE,
  B = 1000L,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

ratings

A units \(\times\) raters matrix (or data.frame). Rows = units of analysis; columns = raters. NA entries are allowed.

level

One of "nominal" (default), "ordinal", "interval", or "ratio"; controls the distance metric used to compute disagreement.

conf_level

Confidence level for the bootstrap CI. Default 0.95.

boot

Logical. If TRUE, fills the interval rows with a bootstrap percentile CI. The default FALSE runs no bootstrap and leaves those rows NA (much faster).

B

Number of bootstrap resamples when boot = TRUE, a single whole number. Default 1000L, because every resample recomputes the coincidences over all pairable values. The fewest accepted is 400 at the default conf_level (200 at 0.90, and 2000 at 0.99, which the default does not meet); a smaller B is refused before anything is computed (class dmar_count_invalid). See Bootstrap replications under Details and dmar_bootstrap.

seed

Optional integer seed for reproducibility of the bootstrap. Default NULL, under which the resamples are drawn from, and advance, the current random number stream; supply an integer for reproducibility, which is set for the call only, the caller's random number state being restored when it returns.

Value

A data.frame (class dmar_tbl) with the same seven rows whatever boot: the point estimate \(\hat\alpha\) (krippendorff_alpha), the observed disagreement \(D_o\) (D_observed), the expected disagreement \(D_e\) (D_expected), the number of pairable values (n_pairable), the lower and upper bootstrap CI limits (ci_lower, ci_upper), and B_used, the number of resamples that returned a finite value and so entered the interval. The last three are NA when boot = FALSE, since no bootstrap was run. With boot = TRUE the table also carries the conf_level attribute (when an interval was formed) and the attributes B, B_used, n_dropped, B_required, and bootstrap_status (see Bootstrap replications under Details).

Details

Coefficient. Krippendorff's \(\alpha\) is $$\alpha \;=\; 1 - \frac{D_o}{D_e},$$ where \(D_o\) is the observed disagreement (average squared distance over all within-unit pairs of ratings, scaled by the number of pairable values), and \(D_e\) is the expected disagreement (average squared distance over all between-unit pairs). The metric used in the squared distance depends on level:

  • nominal: \(d(a, b) = \mathrm{I}(a \ne b)\)

  • ordinal: distance based on cumulative rank counts

  • interval: \(d(a, b) = (a - b)^2\)

  • ratio: \(d(a, b) = ((a - b) / (a + b))^2\)

CI. The CI is by case-resampling bootstrap over units (rows): the rows of ratings are resampled with replacement B times and \(\alpha\) is recomputed on each resample, so units are the sampling unit and the rater panel is treated as fixed. Only the percentile interval is offered: the limits are the empirical quantiles of the bootstrap estimates (Efron & Tibshirani, 1993); there is no bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) variant. When the coefficient is undefined for the data themselves (every value alike), no bootstrap is run and the interval rows stay NA. No closed-form sampling variance is in general use for Krippendorff's alpha across its measurement levels and missing data patterns, so the bootstrap is the interval Krippendorff recommends (Krippendorff, 2011; Hayes & Krippendorff, 2007). B = 1000L typically gives a stable CI to two decimal places. The bootstrap is opt-in (boot = FALSE by default, which returns the point estimate alone and is much faster); ask for it whenever the coefficient is being reported rather than explored, since a point estimate on its own says nothing about how precisely \(\alpha\) is determined.

Bootstrap replications. The two limits are quantiles of the B replicated values of \(\alpha\), so the interval is run only when B puts at least 10 resamples beyond each limit (400 at the 95 percent level). A replication in which \(\alpha\) is undefined (a resample without enough pairable values, or one whose values are all alike, so that the expected disagreement is zero) is dropped and counted, never replaced, and the interval is computed from the rest. The result records B (requested), B_used (the number the interval rests on), n_dropped, and B_required (the fewest replications a request may ask for; that count is held to B, not to B_used) as attributes, and B_used also as a row, with bootstrap_status ("complete", "dropped", "exploratory", "insufficient_count", or "insufficient_share"). One warning of class dmar_bootstrap_replications_dropped states the counts when any replication was dropped, with a caution when the dropped replications are at least the 2.5 percent of B that lies beyond one limit at the 95 percent level, because they could then decide by themselves where that limit falls. When more than half were dropped, the two limit rows are NA, the estimate is returned, and the warning has class dmar_bootstrap_insufficient. options(dmar.bootstrap_exploratory = TRUE) lets a smaller B (2 or more) run for a first look or a demonstration; every such call gives a warning of class dmar_bootstrap_exploratory and the result is not one to report. See dmar_bootstrap for the rule and its reasons. Bootstrap results vary from run to run; supply seed for reproducibility.

Interpretation. \(\alpha\) ranges from \(-D_e / D_o\) (perfect disagreement) through \(0\) (chance level) to \(1\) (perfect agreement). Report the coefficient with its confidence interval and judge it against the reliability the application requires; Krippendorff (2004) discusses how that judgment depends on the cost of acting on unreliable data.

References

Efron, B., & Tibshirani, R. J. (1993). An introduction to the bootstrap. New York, NY: Chapman & Hall/CRC.

Hayes, A. F., & Krippendorff, K. (2007). Answering the call for a standard reliability measure for coding data. Communication Methods and Measures, 1(1), 77–89. doi:10.1080/19312450709336664

Krippendorff, K. (1980). Content analysis: An introduction to its methodology. Sage.

Krippendorff, K. (2004). Content analysis: An introduction to its methodology (2nd ed.). Sage.

Krippendorff, K. (2011). Computing Krippendorff's alpha-reliability. Departmental Papers (ASC), Annenberg School for Communication, University of Pennsylvania.

cohen_kappa, fleiss_kappa, icc

Examples

# 1. Nominal ratings, 4 raters, 12 units (from Krippendorff 2011 Tab. 1):
ratings <- matrix(c(
  1, 2, 3, 3, 2, 1, 4, 1, 2, NA, NA, NA,
  1, 2, 3, 3, 2, 2, 4, 1, 2, 5,  NA, 3,
  NA, 3, 3, 3, 2, 3, 4, 2, 2, 5,  1,  NA,
  1, 2, 3, 3, 2, 4, 4, 1, 2, 5,  1,  NA
), nrow = 12, ncol = 4)
krippendorff_alpha(ratings, level = "nominal")
#>  term               value
#>  krippendorff_alpha 0.743
#>  D_observed         0.200
#>  D_expected         0.779
#>  n_pairable         40   
#>  ci_lower           <NA> 
#>  ci_upper           <NA> 
#>  B_used             <NA> 

# 2. Interval ratings:
set.seed(113)
r1 <- rnorm(30, 0, 1)
r2 <- r1 + rnorm(30, 0, 0.3)
krippendorff_alpha(cbind(r1, r2), level = "interval")
#>  term               value
#>  krippendorff_alpha 0.956
#>  D_observed         0.096
#>  D_expected         2.162
#>  n_pairable         60   
#>  ci_lower           <NA> 
#>  ci_upper           <NA> 
#>  B_used             <NA> 

# The percentile bootstrap interval for the same ratings, which
# recomputes alpha on each of B resamples of the units and fills the
# ci_lower, ci_upper, and B_used rows. B = 400 is the fewest
# resamples a 95 percent interval is reported from and keeps the
# example quick; a reported interval deserves the default B = 1000.
krippendorff_alpha(cbind(r1, r2), level = "interval",
                   boot = TRUE, B = 400L, seed = 113)
#>  term               value
#>  krippendorff_alpha 0.956
#>  D_observed         0.096
#>  D_expected         2.162
#>  n_pairable         60   
#>  ci_lower           0.919
#>  ci_upper           0.975
#>  B_used             400  
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
#> 
#> Bootstrap: 400 replications, 400 used (0 dropped; at least 400 must be requested)
